title: Recurring decimals
competency: Convert recurring decimals to fractions using infinite geometric series.

keywords.def: A decimal with a block of digits that repeats forever.
The number of digits in the repeating block.

en.text: A recurring decimal is an infinite geometric series. 0.474747… = 47/100 + 47/10000 + … with r = 1/100, so it equals (47/100)/(99/100) = 47/99. The quick rule: the repeating digits over as many 9s as there are repeating digits. Add any whole-number part separately.

am.text: ተደጋጋሚ አስርዮሽ ኢውሱን ጂኦሜትሪክ ተከታታይ ድምር ነው። 0.4747… = 47/99። የሚደጋገሙትን አሃዞች በዚያው ብዛት 9ዎች ላይ እንጽፋለን።

Mixed recurring: some digits come first, like 0.1666…

paras: For a purely recurring decimal less than 1:
write the repeating digits on top,

screens.title: The 9s rule, one decimal at a time
screens.ask: Tap each decimal. See the series and the fraction.
items: Mixed: the 1 does not repeat. Split: 1/10 + 6/90 = 1/6. The plain 9s rule does not work here.

screens.ask: Write the recurring decimal 0.565656… as a fraction: ___
screens.why:
Step 1: the block 56 repeats: 2 digits.
Step 2: 0.5656… = 56/100 + 56/10000 + …, so G₁ = 56/100, r = 1/100.
Step 3: S∞ = (56/100)/(99/100) = 56/99.
The 9s rule gives the same: 56 over two 9s.

screens.ask: Write the recurring decimal 3.777… as a fraction: ___
screens.why:
Step 1: split: 3.777… = 3 + 0.777…
Step 2: 0.777… = 7/9 (one repeating digit, one 9).
Step 3: 3 = 27/9, so 27/9 + 7/9 = 34/9.
Check: 34 ÷ 9 = 3.777… ✓. (Trap: 37/9 puts the 3 into the top.)

Step 1: 37/100 = 0.37 exactly. It stops.
Step 2: 0.3737… repeats forever: G₁ = 37/100, r = 1/100.
Step 3: S∞ = (37/100)/(99/100) = 37/99.
So the statement is false. Use 9s, not 10s.

screens.title: Match each decimal to its fraction
screens.text: Match each recurring decimal to the fraction it equals.
screens.why:
0.777…: 1 repeating digit → 7/9.
0.1212…: 2 repeating digits → 12/99.
0.125125…: 3 repeating digits → 125/999.
0.5 stops: it is 5/10 = 1/2, not 5/9.
screens.clue: Count the repeating digits. That many 9s go below.

items.why:
Step 1: one digit repeats: 4.
Step 2: 9s rule: 4 over one 9.
Step 3: 0.444… = 4/9.

Write the recurring decimal 0.565656… as a fraction: ___
items.why:
Step 1: two digits repeat: 56.
Step 2: 9s rule: 56 over two 9s.
Step 3: 0.5656… = 56/99.

test.ask: Write the recurring decimal 0.888… as a fraction: ___
Write the recurring decimal 0.272727… as a fraction: ___
test.why:
Two digits repeat: 27.
9s rule: 27/99.
Divide top and bottom by 9: 3/11.

notes.text: p.42 prints "Mixed requiring decimals"; it should be "Mixed recurring decimals".
The book marks repeating digits with dots (0.4̇7̇). Lessons write 0.474747… because a dot over a digit is hard to read on small screens.

screens.text: Sum to infinity, S∞ = G₁/(1 − r): 8 + 4 + 2 + 1 + … = ?
screens.why:
Step 1: G₁ = 8, r = 4 ÷ 8 = 1/2. |r| < 1 ✓.
Step 2: S∞ = 8/(1 − 1/2) = 8/(1/2).
Step 3: = 16.
(15 is only S₄; the sum never reaches ∞ because the terms halve.)
